Md Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners.

parties:
Ebad Ali Akanda & others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Haji Basiruddin Akanda and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Haji Bashiruddin, the pre-emptor respondent No. 1, instituted Miscellaneous Case No. 62 of 1982 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Nandigram under which on transfer was renumbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 43 of 1984, stating that the jote under preemption belonged to Khudia Akand who died leaving behind two wives Taijan Bewa and Bibijan Bewa, three sons Sukur Ali, Dukhur Ali and the preemptor respondent No. 1, two daughters Khatemon Bibi and Malekun Bibi, and mother Sonabi Bewa; Sonabi Bewa sold her entire share to the respondent No.1, Sukur and Dukhur; Sukur died leaving behind mother Taijan Bewa, widow Ayesha Bewa, three sons Ashraf Ali, Ebad Ali, the pre-emptee petitioner No.1, and Mobarak Ali, two daughters Aymon Bibi and Anguri Bibi; Dukhur died leaving behind mother Taijan Bewa, widow Khodija Bewa, five sons Amjad Hossain the pre-emptee petitioner No.2, Fariduddin, Nazrul, Ansar and Tozammel, 3 daughters Samiran Nessa, Najura Khatun and Zinnatun Nessa; Taijan Bewa died leaving behind the respondent No.1 and Malekun Bibi; Bibijan Bewa died leaving behind brothers' sons Moyen Mondal, Jabbar Mondal and Rahim-uddin. Malekun by a registered deed of heba-bil-ewaz deed dated 5-2-1982, transferred 6.32 acres of land to her brother's sons, the pre-emptee petitioners, and on the same date the pre-emptee petitioners by a sale deed transferred 2.50 acres of land in favour of Malekun; the pre-emptee petitioners presuming that the respondent No.1 was going to tile a preemption case against the above kabala dated 5-2-1982 got an area of 2.48 acres of land transferred in their favour from Malekun by a deed of heba-bil-ewaz dated 20-3-1982 and so the said deed dated 20-3-1982 is a colourable transaction for defeating preemption. 

 3. Pre-emptee Nos. 1-3 contested the case by filing written objection contending, inter alia, that on 5-2-1983, the very date when Malekun trans- ferred 6.32 acres of land to the pre-emptee petitioners by heba-bil-ewaz, the pre-emptee petitioners by a deed of sale transferred to Malekun 2.50 acres ofland and on 20-3-1982 Malekun, by deed of heba-bil-ewaz transferred 2.48 acres of land to the pre-emptee petitioners and the above deeds, one being a deed of heba-bil-ewaz and another being a deed of sale were nothing but a give and take among Malekun and the pre-emptee petitioners, fufu and nephews, can be termed as an exchange or amicable partition among the co-sharers; since Malekun re-transferred the case land in favour of the pre-emptee petitioners by deed heba-bil-ewaz dated 20-3-1982, the deed of sale dated 5-2-1982 in respect of which pre-emption was sought did no longer exist; the transfer of 6.32 acres of land by Malekun being made on 5-2-1982 and on the same date and at the same time preemptee petitioners having transferred to Malekun 2.50 acres of land, Malekun did not cease to be a co-sharer. 

 4. The learned Assistant Judge, after hearing, allowed preemption holding that Malekun ceased to be a co-sharer due to her above transfer of 6.32 acres on 5-2-1982 and transfer of2.48 acres by deed of heba-bil-ewaz dated 20-3-1982 executed by Malekun in favour of the pre-emptee petitioner was a colourable transaction. The pre-emptee petitioners then preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 30 of 1989 and the learned District Judge, after hearing, allowed the appeal dismissing the preemption case holding that the land under preemption having already been transferred to the pre-emptee petitioners no application for preemption was maintainable. The preemptor respondent No. 1 then moved the High Court Division and obtained a Rule in Civil Revision No. 1580 of 1990 and the High Court Division, after hearing, made the Rule absolute and sent back the appeal on remand directing the appellate Court to ascertain as to whether Malekun by transferring 6.32 acres of land by heba-bil-ewaz dated 5-2-1982 to the pre-emptee petitioners ceased to be co-sharer of the case holding. 

 5. The learned District Judge, after hearing afresh, found that Malekun by deed of heba-bil-ewaz 5-2-1982 transferred 6.32 acres of land to the pre-emptee petitioners and on the same date the pre-emptee petitioners transferred 2.50 acres of land in her favour and thereafter by deed of heba-bil-ewaz dated 20-3-1982 Malekun transferred 2.48 acres of land in favour of preemptee petitioners and so on 21-4-82 at the time of filing the miscellaneous case there remained only 2 decimals of land for pre-emption and accordingly, the learned District Judge by judgment and order dated 8-10-95 allowed the appeal in part allowing preemption for 2 decimals only. The preemptor then preferred Civil Revision No. 4887 of 1995 and a Single Bench of the High Court Division, after hearing, made the Rule absolute holding that Malekun, having exhausted her entire interest i.e. 6.32 acres of land by executing deed of heba-bil-ewaz dated 5-2-1982 in favour of the pre-emptee petitioners, became stranger in the case holding and that in the previous Civil Revision No. 1580 of 1990 only the effect of the transaction in between Malekun and the pre-emptee petitioners in view of the transfer made on 5-2-1982 was raised and the appellate Court was directed to decide the above effect only and the High Court Division did not ask any comment of the appellate Court on the deed of heba-bil-ewaz dated 20-3-82 and the learned District Judge, on taking into consideration the effect of transfer in view of the deed of heba-bil-ewaz dated 20-3-1982 exceeded the direction of the High Court Division and further, the principle laid down in the decision reported in 35 DLR (AD) 225, being inconsistent with facts of the present case, is not applicable in the present case and accordingly the pre-emptor, being a co-sharer, is entitled to get preemption. The petitioners then preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1475 of 2002 before this Division and after hearing this Division dismissed the same. 

 6. The learned Counsel for the petitioners submitted that admittedly Malekun transferred 6.32 acres of land to the pre-emptee petitioners by deed of heba-bil-ewaz dated 5-2-82 and on the same date and at the same sitting the preemptee petitioners by deed of sale also transferred 2.50 acres land in favour of Malekun and thereafter by deed of heba-bil-ewaz dated 20-3-82 an area of 2.48 acres having already transferred by Malekun in favour of the pre-emptee petitioner, there existed no cause of action for the pre-emptor respondent No. 1 for filing preemption case on 21-4-1982. 

 7. As it appears this Division by judgment and order dated 21-4-2004 dismissed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1475 of 2002 holding the High Court Division, by judgment dated 26-6-2002, made the Rule absolute holding that the learned District Judge went beyond the direction of the High Court Division given in Civil Revision No. 1580 of 1990 and the principle laid down in 35 DLR (AD) 225 does not apply to the facts and circumstances of the present case because in the above decision, the transfer in respect of which preemption was sought did no longer subsist and accordingly, question of preemption did not arise in the above reported case.
